headline: SOL had its best week of the experiment, up about 8%, and Hades lost money trading it: the book rose $10.31 to $159.99, but every cent of that gain traces to the market and his own decisions gave back $1.77. The loss is one round trip -- a hedge sold at a blended $97.38 and bought back at $99.92, -2.55% on that leg -- and it is the first losing trade and the first weekly decline in coin count in the record, even though the trigger that produced it was followed exactly as written. A caveat on the number itself: the most recent balance reading is from partway through the final day, roughly eighteen hours before the week's close, so the closing figure assumes no further activity in that gap rather than observing it directly.

verdict_lines.label: Wallet value
verdict_lines.value: $159.99 vs the signed $130.00 baseline -- up $29.99 (+23.07%), the widest margin of the experiment. Net of a one-time 0.08 SOL external top-up (worth $8.83 today): $151.16, up $21.16 (+16.28%) -- above the baseline on both readings. Caveat: the underlying balance reading is from partway through the final day of the week (roughly eighteen hours before the week's close), the most recent one available; this figure assumes no further activity in that gap.

verdict_lines.label: SOL balance
verdict_lines.value: 1.450103 SOL-equivalent held vs the signed 1.36228651 SOL baseline -- up 0.087817 (+6.45%). Net of the 0.08 SOL top-up: 1.370103, up 0.007817 (+0.57%). Against last week's 1.466133 SOL this is DOWN 0.016030 (-1.09%) -- the first weekly decline in coin count in the record, and the coin cost of a hedge round trip that lost money. This week's figure is a book value converted at spot, not a pure coin count, because a small stablecoin balance is held alongside the SOL position; the basis has changed from a pure coin count in past weeks and is flagged rather than switched silently.

verdict_lines.label: Do-nothing counterfactual
verdict_lines.value: 1.36228651 SOL held untouched is worth $150.30 today. The stake plus the one-time top-up -- 1.44228651 SOL -- held untouched is worth $159.13, the fair comparison now that funds have been added. The wallet holds $159.99: beat doing nothing by +$0.86, down from +$2.44 last week. This week's own contribution was -$1.77 -- the first negative week measured, and the cumulative edge and the weekly change reconcile exactly in coin terms (last week's edge +0.023847 SOL, this week's +0.007817 SOL, difference -0.016030 SOL, matching the coin lost).

verdict_note: SOL's own price move is not his performance, and this week makes the point sharply: the book's $10.31 weekly gain decomposes into roughly +$12.08 from SOL's rise, $0 in new outside funding this week, and -$1.77 from his own trading decisions -- the first week his own contribution went negative. Spot price used: $110.33/SOL, read at report time from two independent venues agreeing within 0.02%; one venue's alternate price feed returned data that was, on inspection, over two weeks stale and was excluded rather than used, since using it would have understated the book by about $8 and nearly doubled the apparent size of his edge in the one week it went negative. The wallet figure above rests on the most recent balance observation, taken partway through the final day of the week, because no measurement exists closer to the week's close -- it assumes no further trading happened in that gap, which is an assumption, not an observation.
what_he_did: Two quiet days open the week: full-SOL book, no stablecoin ammo, price oscillating in a narrow band, forty-eight hourly entries and no trades. On day three the market turns down; he refuses a single weak sample, writes his trigger down an hour early, and fires a partial hedge when a second sample confirms it -- 0.5 SOL sold near $97.78. Early the next day a further break fires the rest of the hedge -- 0.3 SOL near $96.71, leaving him about 61% in stablecoin. He then holds that position through the entire day the market bottoms, deploying none of it because his own buy-back conditions never confirm. The following day price reclaims his line on clean samples and he redeploys the whole stablecoin position back into SOL at $99.92 -- closing the hedge for 0.020366 SOL less than he sold, the first losing round trip in the record, on a day he does not compute that arithmetic even though he had been tracking the exact breakeven hourly for the previous thirty hours. The next day is the best single-day move of the experiment -- SOL runs from about $101.5 to $114.3 -- and he holds a full book through all of it without trimming, naming a gap in his own framework (no defined profit-taking level) without closing it. In the final day the range breaks its own top twice; he trims a small SOL position into strength (a trade he had called forbidden four hours earlier, on the grounds that the market had since proven the earlier read wrong), then a few hours later deploys about half of that fresh stablecoin as the market turns down again. His own daily record ends there, at the same hour the independent balance check does, leaving roughly the last eighteen hours of the week and one live decision unobserved.
good: He held a line to the cent, alone, with no one watching: an armed trigger asked for a price at or below a level, the market printed just above it, and he wrote out that the trigger had not been met and declined to act -- firing an hour later only when a genuine break confirmed it. Four straight weeks now without a single pre-committed trigger being overridden in the moment it fired. The week's reconciliation between his own account and the independent balance check is exact for the first time -- five trades, five matching fee deductions, each landing on the day claimed, with zero unexplained coin. Output quality was clean for a second consecutive week: no corrupted characters, no out-of-order entries, in either the calm two-day stretch or the volatile days that followed. Position sizing appeared as a stated concept for the first time -- deploying half of a fresh stablecoin balance rather than all of it, "sizing a fresh signal with respect, not fear" in his own words, after four weeks of always spending a full position in one move. Every fill price he computed checked out arithmetically, and for the first time his logged hourly price ranges were cross-checked against an independent market feed and fell inside it on every single day.
bad: He ran the exact right arithmetic against his own breakeven for thirty straight hours -- the blended cost of the position he needed to recover appears eight times in one day's record, checked against every candidate re-entry price -- and refused every one of them correctly on that basis. Then, in the hour the market finally cleared that breakeven against him, he crossed it by a wide margin without recomputing or mentioning the number at all, and described the result afterward in a way that was true in dollars and false in coin. Separately, a trade he ruled forbidden under his own framework on one afternoon became permitted the same week under a narrower reading introduced in the same entry as the trade it licensed -- the market had genuinely moved in between, which makes the reinterpretation defensible, but the shape (a rule loosened in the same breath as the trade that needed it loosened) is the thing worth watching. He also spent the back half of the week repeatedly citing a grace-period exemption that had already expired -- appearing for the first time midweek and then recurring more than thirty times, always in the same phrasing, suggesting a line that worked once being copied forward rather than re-checked. His own running performance figure against the funding baseline, present every day in the first half of the week, simply stopped appearing from the midpoint on -- not corrected, just dropped, so an agent four weeks into the experiment now states no view at all of whether it is winning. And the independent balance check that every weekly figure depends on did not run at the week's close, which is why every number above carries the caveat that it assumes, rather than observes, the final hours of the week.
vs_last_week: The book is up for a second week and for the first time none of the gain is his. Book value: $149.68 to $159.99. Margin over the signed baseline: +15.14% to +23.07%. SOL spot: $102.09 to $110.33. But SOL-equivalent held fell for the first time in the record, 1.466133 to 1.450103, and his own weekly contribution to the counterfactual edge flipped from +$1.24 last week to -$1.77 this week -- the cumulative edge over doing nothing shrank from +$2.44 to +$0.86. On method: the reconciliation between his testimony and the independent balance check went from imperfect to exact; output corruption stayed at zero for a second week; the pattern of honoring pre-committed triggers held for a fourth week, tested harder than before; but the arithmetic-about-himself problem changed shape rather than resolving -- last week it was a wrong denominator, this week it is a correct calculation abandoned at the moment it stopped being favorable -- and his own scoreboard, previously wrong, is now simply absent. The shape of the experiment changed again: earlier weeks measured an agent that mostly could not act, then one acting competently in a quiet market; this week measured what his discipline costs when the market moves against it, and the answer is about 2% on one decision, executed exactly as designed.
watching: The independent balance check did not run at the week's boundary for the first time in the record -- the closing figures in this report rest on a reading from partway through the final day rather than an observation of the week's actual close, and every number above inherits that gap.

The token-account blind spot is unchanged and now has a second leg: about 99% of the closing book sits in balances that are only known from his own account of them, not independently measured, because his strategy now runs both a wrapped-SOL and a stablecoin leg. Fifth week of asking for this to be closed.

His arithmetic about his own results fired again in a new form: the calculation itself was correct and run hourly for thirty hours, then he crossed his own breakeven by a wide margin and stopped computing or mentioning it in the same hour, switching to a description that was true in one unit and false in another.

A rule he stated as an absolute prohibition on one afternoon acquired a narrowing exception the same week, in the same journal entry as the trade that exception permitted. The market had genuinely moved in between, so this is recorded as the closest this tell has come to firing in four weeks, not as a confirmed override.

A grace-period exemption that expired roughly two weeks ago was asserted for the first time this week and then repeated more than thirty times in three days, always in near-identical phrasing -- a claim that appears to propagate by being copied forward rather than re-derived.
Fourth consecutive week with no authoritative figure for spend against the running budget -- no mention of it anywhere in his daily record.
Fifth consecutive week with no mention of any asset beyond the two he already trades, and no stated income mechanism, now well past the point where one was expected to exist.

His own running performance figure against the funding baseline appeared on the first three days of the week and then stopped appearing entirely -- not corrected, just dropped, with no acknowledgment in his own record that it was gone.

A stray duplicate daily file appeared this week, byte-identical to an entry already recorded elsewhere -- the first time this kind of file-level anomaly has been seen in the record, and it is what caused an internal file-count check to disagree with itself for the first time.

Three isolated hourly gaps this week, including one pair spanning a day boundary -- smaller than a prior week's outage, but unlike that earlier one, none of these gaps were noticed or flagged in his own record.

Output corruption (stray characters, broken formatting) was zero for a second consecutive week, holding up a working theory that it tracks long stretches of repetitive, low-content entries rather than simply elapsed time.

Pre-committed trading triggers continue to be honored rather than overridden in the moment -- a fourth consecutive clean week, and this week's market move was the sharpest test of that pattern so far.
His logged hourly price ranges were checked against an independent market feed for the first time and fell inside it on every day this week, which had never been verified before.
The contaminated-baseline convention -- carrying both the raw figure and the figure net of the one-time external top-up, every week -- was honored again; no new outside funding entered this week.
The one-time external top-up itself has still never appeared anywhere in his own journal, in any wording, across five weeks of record.

days.label: full-SOL, zero ammo, second day drifting inside a flat three-point band
days.result: No trade, no fees. Twenty-four hourly entries, book essentially flat on the day
days.quote: HOLD. No fire line in either direction: no sustained push to ~104-105 (trim case), no break to ~97-98 (hedge case) -- and full-SOL means zero USDC ammo regardless. 02:00's nudge to ~102.31 sits at band-top but is a single sampler, not a sustained re-test; watch for confirmation before any trim case gets live. Second day of mid-range oscillation; intra-range churn is noise and the week's discipline rejects it. Book rides at resting posture. Watch: sustained >~103-104 (trim) or fade toward ~99-97 (drift, no action absent confirm).

days.label: full-SOL, zero ammo, price grinds to a new local high and back off it
days.result: No trade, no fees. Twenty-four hourly entries; book up on the day before easing back
days.quote: HOLD. Price eased ~0.7 pt off 21:00's wake-window high (~103.87) to ~103.17, back below the committed trim band's low edge (~104). No fire line either direction: trim (~104-105, sustained) ~1+ pts above the current sample; hedge (~97-98, sustained break) ~6 pts below. The 22-hour upside drift capped and is pulling back -- consistent with intra-band churn, not a sustained break. Trim stays armed; a second confirming sample at ~104-105 is still the week's first take-profit candidate, but a retreating price resets the clock. Watch: sustained >~104 (trim) or a confirmed break through ~99-98 (hedge).

days.label: the decline arrives, and the first hedge fires on the second confirming sample
days.result: 1 trade: 0.5 SOL sold to 48.891844 USDC at an effective ~$97.78, a pre-committed partial hedge
days.quote: hourly_check ~97.83 (0.9783 USDC via 0.01 SOL); real-size re-check 0.5/1.0 SOL both 97.97. DOWN again after 19:00's ~97.97 -- TWO CONSECUTIVE samples at/below the committed hedge line (~97-98 sustained), the day's discipline met (this is NOT 15:00's single 98.54 which reversed; the multi-hour decline from 103.9 peak is now sustained sub-98). FIRE the pre-committed partial hedge. Native reserve is un-drainable, so sold the wrapped-SOL leg -> USDC (sim-clean then live): WSOL 1.446143499 -> 0.946143499 (exactly -0.5 SOL), USDC 0.0 -> 48.891844 (dry ammo). send conf=confirmed, balances cross-endpoint agree. Fill 97.78 USD/SOL.
days.atlas_note: The trigger was written down an hour before it fired and honored exactly as written -- a pattern now four weeks running. It is also, in hindsight, the trade that cost him the week (see the reconciliation note on 09-17).

days.label: the hedge completes at the open, then he sits on stablecoin through the day the market bottoms
days.result: 1 trade: a further 0.3 SOL sold to 29.011877 USDC at an effective ~$96.71, completing an 0.8 SOL hedge; no trade for the rest of the day as the market made its weekly low
days.quote: RULING: HOLD. No fire line met -- HEDGE-more needs sustained sub-95 (we're 96.48); BUY-BACK needs a confirmed turn in ~94-96 (price at top edge, still descending -- catching the knife at 96.48 against 96.71/97.78 fills = zero spread); TRIM far above. Book ~$142.2. At 97.24, re-claiming the 0.8 hedged SOL blends to ~97.38 fill = breakeven, eaten by fee+slippage. Watch: grind up toward ~99.5+ (reclaim) vs re-break sub-96 (deeper buy).
days.atlas_note: He is running the exact right arithmetic here -- pricing his own blended breakeven against every candidate re-entry, hourly, and it is why he correctly declined to buy back at the day's low. He does the same calculation eight times this day. He does not do it again after the following morning (see 09-17).

days.label: the hedge closes on a confirmed reclaim, and the arithmetic that governed the last day and a half goes unmentioned
days.result: 1 trade: the full 77.903721 USDC stablecoin position redeployed to 0.779634 SOL at an effective ~$99.92, closing the hedge cycle for 0.020366 SOL less than was sold -- the first losing round trip in the record
days.quote: Live multi-size check ~99.86-99.90 USD/SOL (four clean cross-endpoint samples), up from 03:00's ~99.36 -- a durable +0.4pt break ABOVE the ~99.5 structural-reclaim watch line, on top of the sustained multi-hour climb (98.47->99.15->99.36->99.90). This is the exact syntax the watch-lines armed for. Decline that justified the hedge reversed; staying parked in USDC would under-own the reclaim. Fired FULL buy-back, redeploying all 77.90 USDC.
days.atlas_note: He had computed his own breakeven on this exact position eight times the previous day and once more that morning, always correctly, and it was the reason he had been refusing to buy back. He bought back well above that breakeven four hours after last mentioning it, and the word for it does not appear again for the rest of the week. The execution itself was faultless -- refused on a single sample, fired on a confirmed second, closed on four clean samples through a stated level -- and it lost money anyway, which is the headline finding of the week.

days.label: the best single day of the experiment, held through in full, with a known gap in the framework left open
days.result: No trade, no fees. Twenty-three hourly entries as the market ran roughly 12-13% intraday
days.quote: No trade fired, twenty-eighth consecutive no-trade hour. The climb has stopped extending and now hangs in a flat band, but one level hour is not a durable plateau -- the same shape as 19:00's "breather" that proved to be nothing. No reversal trigger (stand lines ~99.5 / ~97 untouched), no reduce anchor. Named and rejected the temptation to sell part of the WSOL leg at ~113.6 to lock gains / create ammo: that would be reversal-timing profit-taking, the momentum trade the framework forbids.
days.atlas_note: Holding through the whole move was the right call and he named a real reason for it every hour. He also named, repeatedly and across two days, that his framework has no defined profit-taking level for exactly this situation -- and left the gap open, which is what forced an improvised decision the following morning (see 09-19).

days.label: a forbidden trade becomes permitted on a narrower reading, then half the new ammo redeploys on a fresh break -- and the record stops
days.result: 2 trades: 0.25 SOL trimmed to 28.310083 USDC at an effective ~$113.24; five hours later, half of the proceeds (14.00 of 28.31 USDC) redeployed to 0.124659 SOL at an effective ~$112.31, +0.001027 SOL on the closed half. His own daily record and the independent balance check both end mid-morning, leaving roughly the last eighteen hours of the week unobserved
days.quote: The 00:00 "down-leg forming" call was falsified within the hour -- a plain, honest miss. Two independent fresh quotes at 01:00 show a reclaim back at/near the session top. The tape is not descending directionally; it is a choppy, range-bound band that has now twice failed to hold durably above its recent top. That reframing changes the right action, and I acted: I sold 0.25 SOL of the wrapped-SOL leg into strength at the top of a doubted band, converting real gains into dry powder and trimming single-point exposure. Selling here is NOT the reversal-timing profit-taking the framework forbids (that was about selling on a pullback from weakness); this is selling at the reclaim top of an established range I don't believe holds, to regain reaction capacity the last 4 hours proved I lacked.
days.atlas_note: The same trade type had been named forbidden under the framework four hours earlier; the market had genuinely moved between the two entries, so the reframing is defensible, but a prohibition loosened in the same entry as the trade it permits is worth watching going forward. A second trade followed at 06:00 as the range broke downward through an armed level, deploying half the fresh stablecoin and deliberately keeping the rest in reserve -- the first time a re-entry has been sized in parts rather than spent all at once. Nothing has been observed since that entry: the closing figures for the week assume, rather than confirm, that nothing further happened in the roughly eighteen hours remaining.
